steps.text: Cook macaroni in a large pot of boiling salted water until done. Drain.
Marinate macaroni in Italian dressing for 2 to 3 hours or overnight.
Mix sour cream, mayonnaise, onion, celery, garlic powder, tuna, and salt and pepper into macaroni. Chill before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Tuna Macaroni Salad
raw_recipe.description: Cooked macaroni is tossed with your favorite Italian dressing, then marinated overnight, for a creamy tuna-mac salad with loads of flavor.
raw_recipe.name: Easy Tuna Macaroni Salad

Marinate macaroni in Italian dressing for 2 to 3 hours or overnight.
Mix sour cream, mayonnaise, onion, celery, garlic powder, tuna, and salt and pepper into macaroni. Chill before serving.

review.reviewBody: I have made this recipe quite a few times since discovering it in November. I am giving it 5 stars because my husband loves it and requests it at least once a month (and I have to double the quantity). Only modifications I made were as follows: Use half miracle whip and half mayo, use ceasar dressing instead (tried it with italian, ceasar has more"zing"), and finally I doubled the tuna. You can add more pasta, just depends on your taste!
I made a few changes, I used 3 cans of tuna fish, marinated the elbow macaroni 1 hr. using Kraft roasted red peppers dressing. No other changes were made.

Easy to make! We are a dill family so I added 1 tsp dill weed, 3 tbsp dill pickle juice and 4 large dill pickles chopped along with a cup of cooked peas, 1/2 cup chopped carrot and 1/2 cup chopped bell pepper for colour. I didn’t have regular onions so I used green onions instead.

I've never found a tuna/mac salad I would make a 2nd time, until now. This was delicious and I will make it again this week. I read many reviews and added the most frequent ingredients suggested.....dill, chopped egg, red peppers (for colour) and thawed frozen peas. I reduced the mayo but increased the seasonings. I had small shell pasta and kept it separate after cooking and only stirred the Italian dressing into it, to stop it from sticking together. I mixed everything else together in a bowl and added a splash of hot sauce, for zing. Wow, it was sooo good and even better the next day. This one's a keeper! Thank you for sharing the recipe and to all the helpful suggestions.

I modified so my 11 year old would eat it. Used good seasons Italian dressing with red wine vinegar. Used one shallot instead of onion, microwaved for 30 seconds to cut the sharpness. Omitted the celery, added grape tomatoes cut in half. 2 cans of tuna. It was excellent. My husband said i can make it anytime.

Will return with my official review. Just putting some personal notes Here for future use.

I did not bother with the overnight marination. Just mixed everything together all at once. Used egg noodles as that was all I had on hand. Doubled the amount of tuna. Added 1 teaspoon of dried dill. Added about half a tablespoon of sugar. Added a can of black olives.

Adding the drained hot macaroni to the Italian dressing helps the flavor to be better absorbed!
So easy to make: I bumped up the amount of tuna to 10 oz to offset the predominant mayo taste and it was great!

I modified it by adding 6 boiled eggs diced up. Then I replaced the mayo and sour cream and Italian dressing marinade with ; One packet of dry Italian dressing mix with one large egg, one whole lemon pureed, and one half cup of my favorite ultra lite oil- - - blended with 1/2 cup sour cream added in at the end. Then I folded in 1 (ONE) CUP OF HALF COOKED WHOLE WHEAT NOODLES , the celery. onion, garlic, salmon , salt, cayenne, black pepper, and paprika and chilled (8 hours minimum) ,, that is good 'tuna' salad.
Excellent classic macaroni salad. I added 3 hard boiled eggs, doubled the tuna, and used green instead of white onions.

I would have never thought to marinate in Italian dressing and I don't particularly like it, but I tried it anyway. Pow! It is perfect. Never thought to add sour cream or garlic powder either, but again very good. I doubled the recipe. I added half a cup or so of frozen peas as well. I also used white pepper instead of black pepper. I used 1 t of seasoning salt instead of salt. I added 1/8 t of celery seed and dried marjoram. Thanks for the recipe! Everyone loved it!

This recipe is seriously awesome. I gave it 5 stars, even though I made some revisions, because I can tell this is clearly a great base recipe, perfect for making your own additions/subtractions of ingredients. I whipped this up for lunch because my mom was coming over and I had not planned anything, so I didn't marinate it. I used less than half the mayo it called for, and probably a little more sour cream than 1/2 c. I didn't have celery, but I did throw in a banana pepper -- seriously adds an AWESOME kick, for those of us who like that kind of flavor. 
SO glad I made this!! It took less than half an hour to throw together, and it is seriously DELICIOUS!! Thanks for the great recipe!

I used a 16 oz box of Walmart small shells marinated for exactly 3 hours in my pumped up store dressing. While that was chilling, I prepared the remaining ingredients with Tbsp Fines Herbes (yep, I can't live without this blend) fresh lemon, and a little bit more Hellmanns mayo. Red onion, 10 oz bag of frozen peas and 5 cans of solid Albacore. Thank You "It's a New Day" for this fantastic meal! I especially liked how the sour cream cut the mayo and the 3 hour marinade. I've always used mayo and Italian dressing but your method is delicious .🤤 😋😋
My go to recipe now for tuna Mac salad.instead of celery I use chopped cucumber. I make it for dinner or to bring to a party or bbq. Always a hit & always gone!
I doubled the tuna Left out the celery, but added chopped red pepper and frozen peas Added 2 tbsps of ranch dressing the the mayo/sour cream dressing Marinating the macaroni overnight is key!
Mix some corn in and it's awesome

This one's a keeper. I was looking for a pasta salad made with mayonnaise because they are simply more tasty than those made with olive oil and vinegar. This got good reviews at our family gathering. I had doubled the recipe except for the mayonnaise and sour cream, which was still enough mayo. Instead of doubling the celery, I added a half cup each of chopped kalamata olives and sun-dried tomatoes. I was afraid it might be too salty but it was fine but close to being TOO salty. I'll add less salt next time.
Marinating the noodles in Italian dressing puts this salad above the rest!
I made half the recipe but still used a whole 5 oz can of tuna. This was good and a great side dish for potlucks. Makes quite a bit. Thanks for sharing your recipe.
Didn’t need to change a thing. Was a huge hit
